sections.text: The time and date, written as the state of two qubits.

sections.caption: Drag to turn the sphere. Double-click to reset the view.

sections.title: If you measured now
sections.note: Measuring collapses each qubit to |0⟩ or |1⟩. The dashed rings on the sphere mark these odds: every point on a ring has the same chance.

modes.label: Rotations
modes.caption: Start in |0⟩, tilt down by θ with an R<sub>y</sub> rotation, then turn by φ around the z-axis with R<sub>z</sub>. This is exact, up to a global phase.

modes.label: One U gate
modes.caption: U(θ, φ, λ) is the general single-qubit gate, so one gate can do both rotations. Its third angle λ would only add a global phase to |0⟩, so it is set to 0.

modes.label: Clifford + T
modes.caption: Real quantum hardware runs a small, fixed set of gates. This is the shortest sequence of H, S, T, Z and their inverses found that reaches each state with fidelity of at least 0.999, searching up to seven H gates. Where none gets there, it is the closest one found.
